turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning from Device Physics

I'm looking for the combination of features that consistently produced the highest efficiencies (>19-23%) in the training set.

**Key patterns from training data:**

1. **Composition matters most.** The top tier (19–23%) is dominated by **FAMAPbBrI** and **CsFAMAPbBrI** triple/quadruple-cation mixed-halide absorbers (~1.55–1.6 eV, ideal bandgap, defect-tolerant, good film quality). Pure narrow-gap Sn or Sn–Pb, wide-gap CsPbBr, and Bi/Sb absorbers are all low. FAMAPbI (pure iodide, ~1.5 eV) also reaches 19–20%.

2. **n-i-p with SnO2 or TiO2-mp ETL + Spiro-MeOTAD + Au** is the workhorse of the highest efficiencies. SnO2 gives excellent band alignment/low interface recombination; Au is the ideal inert high-work-function contact for Spiro. Interface passivation/modifier layers (SrCl2, trimethylamine oxide, OAI/DM, secondary amines) push into the 20–23% range.

3. **PIN with PTAA (or NiO) + C60/PCBM + Cu/Ag** also reaches ~18–20%, but PEDOT:PSS-based PIN caps lower (~13–16%) due to its low work function/interface losses.

**Scoring the pool candidates for these winning motifs:**

- **c099** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, FTO/TiO2-c|TiO2-mp, Au-nw|Spiro-MeOTAD, Au. Ideal composition + mesoporous TiO2 + Spiro/Au + a plasmonic/passivating Au-nw modifier. Top motif. **Very high.**
- **c019** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, TiO2-mp, **DM**, Au. DM is exactly the HTL that gave the 22.9% champion (OAI|DM). Excellent. **Very high.**
- **c047** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SnO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au. Clean SnO2 planar + Spiro/Au — matches many ~19–20% rows.
- **c055** — FAMAPbBrI, nip, SnO2-c, SWCNTs|Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag. SnO2 + composite HTL; strong.
- **c008** — FAMAPbI, nip, SnO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au. Matches 18.5% row exactly (SnO2/Spiro/Au FAMAPbI).
- **c010** — FAMAPbI, nip, TiO2-mp, Spiro, Ag — good but Ag contact slightly weaker.
- **c057/c063** — good comp + dopant-free HTLs (X25/TT0) — solid but novel HTLs are riskier.

The two candidates carrying the exact "champion" fingerprints — **DM HTL** (c019) and **passivated Spiro/Au on mp-TiO2** (c099) — plus the reliable SnO2/Spiro/Au FAMAPbBrI cells stand out.

**Final: c019, c099, c047, c055, c008**
